title: TAI 307
summary: The DC-7C departed Bordeaux at night with light drizzle and limited visibility. Following takeoff, the aircraft reached only 30 m altitude and failed to climb further before flying into a pine forest 2950 m from the runway. The aircraft cut a swath through the forest, and the fuselage broke up before post-crash fire destroyed the wreckage.
probable_cause: With lack of visual references in darkness, the pilot failed to maintain optimum climbing speed and did not carefully monitor the altimeter, allowing the aircraft to descend back to terrain level.

factors.evidence: Darkness and a lack of visual references led the crew to have difficulty maintaining awareness of the aircraft's position and altitude.
Evidence from a reconstructed flight showed the rate of climb would decrease if optimum climbing speed was not maintained.
A pilot may follow a line of flight that will bring the aircraft back near the ground if the altimeter is not carefully watched.
The aircraft flew into a pine forest located 2950 m from the end of the runway after reaching only 30 m altitude.

events.text: Departure from Bordeaux with light drizzle and 3 knot wind
Aircraft fails to maintain climb rate, altitude plateaus at 30 meters
Aircraft enters pine forest 2,950 meters from runway end, wings impact trees
Fuselage breaks up, post-crash fire, rescue hampered by darkness and terrain
